findings.description: The bucket has no server_side_encryption_configuration block, meaning objects stored in it are not encrypted at rest by default, risking data exposure if underlying storage or backups are compromised.

findings.issue_category: no bucket ACL / public access controls defined
findings.description: No ACL or public access block is specified, so the bucket could default to being more permissive than intended and is not explicitly restricted from public access.
This bucket stores sensitive ledger export data but has no server_side_encryption_configuration, leaving data unencrypted at rest.
The bucket lacks a server_side_encryption_configuration block, so model artifacts are stored unencrypted at rest.
The bucket lacks a server_side_encryption_configuration block, so operational runbook data (potentially containing sensitive operational details) is stored unencrypted.

The acl value 'lcatalogopts-delivery-write' is not a valid S3 canned ACL; if Terraform coerces or a similar valid-looking ACL such as 'log-delivery-write' is intended, it could grant broad write/read permissions to the S3 log delivery group, and as written this misconfiguration could cause unpredictable access control behavior for an audit log bucket that should be tightly restricted.

findings.issue_category: plaintext storage of potentially sensitive data
findings.description: The vendor roster file is uploaded to the reports_archive bucket which has no encryption configuration, meaning potentially sensitive vendor data is stored without encryption at rest and without an explicit ACL restricting access.

findings.issue_category: force_destroy enabled on bucket with no versioning
findings.description: force_destroy is set to true and there is no versioning configuration, so accidental or malicious deletion of the bucket will permanently destroy all contained objects with no recovery path, increasing impact of an attacker or operator error.

force_destroy is true and no versioning block is defined, meaning ledger export data can be irrecoverably deleted, which is particularly risky for financial ledger data that may need to be preserved for integrity/audit purposes.
